object_description: raised pavilion with two introverted classroom levels and numerous interior patios
design_condition: The building follows Cours Roger-Bonvin and occupies the site without residual spaces, raising its ground floor above natural terrain and creating a covered perimeter threshold toward the landscape and city.

positive.statement: The covered outdoor space creates a link between the exterior and interior as a large threshold.

position.rationale: Perimeter threshold is approximated along the south-facing lower edge connecting exterior and interior.

positive.statement: The generous ground floor opens toward the city as a space for communication and exchange.

position.rationale: Ground-floor openness is anchored to the raised lower perimeter and broad accessible base.

positive.statement: The two-stage spatiality offers a new way of designing an educational space.

position.rationale: The marker represents the stacked lower and introverted upper educational volumes.

positive.statement: The innovative and daring proposal shakes up thinking about secondary-level learning.

position.rationale: Judgment concerns the proposal’s educational identity rather than a locatable geometric feature.

positive.statement: The project’s courage and innovation enabled debate on the college of tomorrow.

position.rationale: Comment addresses innovation and debate at project scale without a specific spatial referent.

negative.statement: The installation occupies the land without leaving residual spaces.

position.rationale: Site occupation is anchored to the building footprint and its perimeter condition at ground level.

negative.statement: The building reinforces the urban path without completely connecting to it.

position.rationale: Incomplete connection is approximated at the lower south-west perimeter threshold.

negative.statement: The glass-block classroom walls are interesting but not well suited to the use of these spaces.

position.rationale: Classroom wall placement is approximated on the upper north-east envelope; material is not distinguishable.

negative.statement: The corridors leading to the classrooms are undersized for the number of students moving simultaneously.

position.rationale: Interior corridors are inferred near the upper-level central circulation zone, adjacent to visible classroom patterns.

negative.statement: The spatial proposal seems more suitable for a university-level establishment than a secondary school.

position.rationale: Programmatic criticism applies broadly, anchored to the building’s stacked educational mass.
